name: Titanium.Gesture
summary:
The Gesture module is responsible for high-level device gestures such as orientation changes
and shake gestures.

properties.name: landscape
properties.summary: Indicates if the device is currently held in landscape form.
properties.description: Value is `true` if in landscape, and `false` otherwise.

properties.name: orientation
properties.description:
Value may be one of the group of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI) orientation constants,
[Titanium.UI.PORTRAIT](api:Titanium.UI#PORTRAIT),
[Titanium.UI.UPSIDE_PORTRAIT](api:Titanium.UI#UPSIDE_PORTRAIT),
[Titanium.UI.LANDSCAPE_LEFT](api:Titanium.UI#LANDSCAPE_LEFT),
[Titanium.UI.LANDSCAPE_RIGHT](api:Titanium.UI#LANDSCAPE_RIGHT),
[Titanium.UI.FACE_UP](api:Titanium.UI#FACE_UP),
[Titanium.UI.FACE_DOWN](api:Titanium.UI#FACE_DOWN),
or [Titanium.UI.UNKNOWN](api:Titanium.UI#UNKNOWN).

On iOS and Windows, returns the current orientation of the *device*,
regardless of the window orientation. To determine the current window orientation,
use [Window.orientation](api:Titanium.UI.Window#orientation).

To set the *allowable* orientations for a window, see [Titanium.UI.Window.orientationModes](api:Titanium.UI.Window#orientationModes).

properties.name: portrait
properties.summary: Indicates if the device is currently held in portrait form.
properties.description: Value is `true` if in portrait, and `false` otherwise.

methods.name: stopListener
methods.description:
In case you use `Titanium.Gesture.landscape` or `Titanium.Gesture.portrait` it will attach the orientation
listener automatically. If you just use it once you can use this method to stop the listener.

events.name: orientationchange
events.summary: Fired when the device orientation changes.
events.description:
On Android, note that the application must have a heavyweight window or tab group open
in order to receive the `orientationchange` event. It is not necessary for the  heavyweight
window to be the topmost window.

Almost all real-world applications will have a heavyweight window or a tab group. This is
only likely to be an issue if you create a test case or test application that adds an
orientation change listener from `app.js` without opening a heavyweight window.

events.name: shake
events.summary: Fired when the device is shaken.
events.description:
A shake gesture consists of a series of quick accelerations, and is represented by a series
of shake events.

The `timestamp` property represents the interval between shake events. It is measured in
milliseconds on Android, and in seconds on iOS.

properties.name: timestamp
properties.summary:
Time interval since previous shake event. On iOS, this value is 0 for the first shake
event in a series.

properties.name: x
properties.summary: Acceleration along the X axis, in Gs.

properties.name: y
properties.summary: Acceleration along the Y axis, in Gs.

properties.name: z
properties.summary: Acceleration along the Z axis, in Gs.
